101.solution: Separating, \(\dfrac{1}{y+1}\,dy=\dfrac{-\cos x}{2+\sin x}\,dx\). Integrating: \(\log(y+1)=-\log(2+\sin x)+c\). At \(x=0,\ y=1\): \(\log 2=-\log 2+c\Rightarrow c=\log 4\). So \(y+1=\dfrac{4}{2+\sin x}\). At \(x=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\): \(y=\dfrac{4}{3}-1=\dfrac13\).

103.solution: From \(|\bar a+\bar b|^2+|\bar a+\bar c|^2=8\): \(4+2(\bar a\cdot\bar b+\bar a\cdot\bar c)=8\Rightarrow \bar a\cdot\bar b+\bar a\cdot\bar c=2\). Then \(|\bar a+3\bar b|^2+|\bar a+3\bar c|^2=20+6(\bar a\cdot\bar b+\bar a\cdot\bar c)=20+12=32\).

105.subtopic: Section Formula, Concurrency, Foot of Perpendicular, and Distance
105.solution: Distance of \(ax+by+c=0\) from origin \(=\dfrac{|c|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}\). (A) \(\dfrac4{5}=0.8\); (B) \(\dfrac5{\sqrt{13}}\approx1.39\); (C) \(\dfrac{12}{5}=2.4\); (D) \(\dfrac3{\sqrt{29}}\approx0.557\). The least is option (D).

106.solution: \([p\wedge\sim r]\to(\sim r\wedge q)\equiv F\Rightarrow p\wedge\sim r\equiv T\) and \(\sim r\wedge q\equiv F\). So \(p\equiv T,\ r\equiv F\); with \(\sim r\equiv T\), \(q\equiv F\). Check (D): \(\sim(r\vee q)\to\sim p=\sim(F\vee F)\to\sim T=T\to F\equiv F\).

107.subtopic: Scalar Triple Product, Coplanarity, and Volume
107.solution: Let \(\bar d=p\hat i+q\hat j+r\hat k\). Coplanarity \([\bar b\ \bar c\ \bar d]=0\) gives \(p+q+r=0\); \(\bar a\cdot\bar d=0\) gives \(p-q=0\Rightarrow p=q\). Option (D) \(\dfrac{\hat i+\hat j-2\hat k}{\sqrt6}\) satisfies both (\(1+1-2=0\), \(p=q=1\)) and is a unit vector.

108.subtopic: Properties of Triangles — Sine/Cosine Rules and Projection
108.solution: Cosine rule: \(a^2+b^2-c^2=2ab\cos C\); squaring and using \(a^4+b^4+c^4=2a^2c^2+2b^2c^2\) gives \(2a^2b^2=4a^2b^2\cos^2 C\Rightarrow\cos^2 C=\dfrac12\Rightarrow\cos C=\pm\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\). The only matching option is \(C=135^\circ\).

111.solution: Both lines have direction \((2,3,4)\), so they are parallel; the square's side equals the distance between them. \((\bar r_2-\bar r_1)=(-1,3,-4)\); \((\bar r_2-\bar r_1)\times\bar d=(24,-4,-9)\), magnitude \(\sqrt{673}\); \(|\bar d|=\sqrt{29}\). Side \(=\dfrac{\sqrt{673}}{\sqrt{29}}\), so perimeter \(=\dfrac{4\sqrt{673}}{\sqrt{29}}\) units.

112.subtopic: Properties of Triangles — Sine/Cosine Rules and Projection
112.solution: By Napier's analogy, \(\tan\left(\dfrac{B-C}2\right)=\dfrac{b-c}{b+c}\cot\dfrac A2\). Comparing with \(x\cot\dfrac A2\) gives \(x=\dfrac{b-c}{b+c}\).

113.subtopic: Probability Distribution — Constants, Expectation, and Variance

114.subtopic: Order, Degree, Formation of ODE, and Verification of Solutions
114.solution: The equation contains \(\log\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)\), so it cannot be written as a polynomial in the derivatives. Hence the degree is not defined.

115.solution: Sum of squares of distances from the three axes \(=(y^2+z^2)+(x^2+z^2)+(x^2+y^2)=2(x^2+y^2+z^2)=324\Rightarrow x^2+y^2+z^2=162\). Distance from origin \(=\sqrt{162}=9\sqrt2\).

116.subtopic: Symmetry, King's Property, and Absolute Value
116.solution: For \(i=0,1,\dots,49\): \(\dfrac12\le\dfrac12+\dfrac i{100}<1\Rightarrow\) floor \(=0\). For \(i=50,\dots,99\): \(1\le\dfrac12+\dfrac i{100}<2\Rightarrow\) floor \(=1\), giving 50 terms. Total \(=50\).

117.subtopic: Angles — Line, Plane, and Direction Conditions
117.solution: \(3x=2y=-z\Rightarrow\dfrac x2=\dfrac y3=\dfrac z{-6}\); \(-x=6y=-4z\Rightarrow\dfrac x{-12}=\dfrac y2=\dfrac z{-3}\). \(a_1a_2+b_1b_2+c_1c_2=2(-12)+3(2)+(-6)(-3)=-24+6+18=0\). Lines are perpendicular, so the angle is \(\dfrac\pi2\).

118.solution: \(y+\dfrac{d}{dx}(xy)=x(\sin x+\log x)\Rightarrow x\dfrac{dy}{dx}+2y=x(\sin x+\log x)\Rightarrow\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac2x y=\sin x+\log x\). I.F. \(=x^2\). Then \(yx^2=\int(x^2\sin x+x^2\log x)\,dx=-x^2\cos x+2x\sin x+2\cos x+\dfrac{x^3}3\log x-\dfrac{x^3}9+c\). Dividing by \(x^2\): \(y=-\cos x+\dfrac2x\sin x+\dfrac2{x^2}\cos x+\dfrac x3\log x-\dfrac x9+\dfrac c{x^2}\).

119.subtopic: Combined Equation and Condition for Pair of Lines
119.solution: \(xy-x+y-1=(x+1)(y-1)=0\), so the lines meet at \((-1,1)\). For concurrency, \(x+ky-3=0\) passes through it: \(-1+k-3=0\Rightarrow k=4\).

120.subtopic: Continuity at a Point — Finding Parameters

121.solution: (A) sum of cube roots of unity is \(0\neq1\), so the conjunction is F. (B) \(11>10\) (T) iff \(10<10\) (F): \(T\leftrightarrow F\equiv F\). (C) \(x^2-3x+2=0\) has \(x=1,2\in\mathbb N\) and an odd \(n\) exists: \(T\wedge T\equiv T\). (D) \(3+i\) is complex (T) or \(\sqrt2+\sqrt3=\sqrt5\) (F): \(T\vee F\equiv T\). True statements are (C) and (D).

122.subtopic: Probability Distribution — Constants, Expectation, and Variance

123.solution: \(\dfrac{dP}{dt}=kP\Rightarrow\log\left(\dfrac{P}{40000}\right)=kt\). From \(t=20,\ P=80000\): \(20k=\log2\). The further 40 years means \(t=60\): \(\log\left(\dfrac{P}{40000}\right)=3\log2\Rightarrow P=40000\cdot8=320000\).

124.subtopic: Scalar Triple Product, Coplanarity, and Volume
124.solution: Coplanarity \(\Rightarrow\begin{vmatrix}m&m&n\\1&0&1\\n&n&p\end{vmatrix}=0\Rightarrow -mn-mp+mn+n^2=0\Rightarrow n^2=mp\). Hence \(m,n,p\) are in G.P.

125.subtopic: Trig Identities, Compound Angle, and Equations
125.solution: Terms run \(\sin^2 5^\circ,\dots,\sin^2 90^\circ\) (step \(5^\circ\), 18 terms). Pairing \(\sin^2\theta+\sin^2(90^\circ-\theta)=1\) gives 8 pairs \((5,85),\dots,(40,50)=8\); the middle term \(\sin^2 45^\circ=\dfrac12\) and \(\sin^2 90^\circ=1\). Total \(=8+\dfrac12+1=\dfrac{19}2\).

126.subtopic: Area Bounded by Curves, Axes, and Lines

128.subtopic: Symmetry, King's Property, and Absolute Value
128.solution: By \(x\to\pi-x\), \(2I=\pi\int_{\pi/3}^{2\pi/3}\dfrac{dx}{1+\sin x}=\pi\int_{\pi/3}^{2\pi/3}(\sec^2 x-\sec x\tan x)\,dx=\pi[\tan x-\sec x]_{\pi/3}^{2\pi/3}=\pi[(-\sqrt3+2)-(\sqrt3-2)]=2\pi(2-\sqrt3)\). Hence \(I=\pi(2-\sqrt3)\).

130.subtopic: Trigonometric Integrals - Rational and Substitution Forms

131.solution: \(\cos2x-\cos2\alpha=2(\cos^2 x-\cos^2\alpha)=2(\cos x-\cos\alpha)(\cos x+\cos\alpha)\). So \(\int\dfrac{\cos2x-\cos2\alpha}{\cos x-\cos\alpha}\,dx=2\int(\cos x+\cos\alpha)\,dx=2\sin x+2x\cos\alpha+c\).

132.solution: Choose 12 of 21 for the first table and arrange round both tables: \(\binom{21}{12}\times11!\times8!=\dfrac{21!}{12!\,9!}\times11!\times8!=\dfrac{21!}{12\cdot9}=\dfrac{35}{9}\times19!\).

133.solution: Area \(=\dfrac12|\bar d_1\times\bar d_2|\) where \(\bar d_1=2\bar a-\bar b,\ \bar d_2=4\bar a-5\bar b\). \(\bar d_1\times\bar d_2=-6(\bar a\times\bar b)\), and \(|\bar a\times\bar b|=\sin45^\circ=\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\). Area \(=\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac6{\sqrt2}=\dfrac3{\sqrt2}\) sq. units.

135.subtopic: Inverse Trigonometric Functions — Identities, Equations, Principal Values, and Sums

136.subtopic: Algebraic Equations, Locus, and Cube Roots
136.solution: \(\left|\dfrac{z+i}{z-i}\right|=\sqrt3\Rightarrow x^2+(y+1)^2=3[x^2+(y-1)^2]\Rightarrow x^2+(y-2)^2=3\). This is a circle with centre \((0,2)\) and radius \(\sqrt3\).

137.solution: Writing \(\dfrac{2x^2+3}{(x^2-1)(x^2-4)}=\dfrac{11/3}{x^2-4}-\dfrac{5/3}{x^2-1}\) and integrating gives \(\dfrac{11}{12}\log\left|\dfrac{x-2}{x+2}\right|+\dfrac56\log\left|\dfrac{x+1}{x-1}\right|+c\). So \(a=\dfrac{11}{12},\ b=\dfrac56\) and \(a+b=\dfrac{11}{12}+\dfrac{10}{12}=\dfrac{21}{12}\).

139.subtopic: Basic Probability — Events, Conditional, and Complement

141.subtopic: Tangent, Normal, Approximation, and Curve from Geometric Condition

142.subtopic: Conic Properties — Eccentricity, Orthogonality, and Intersection
142.solution: Tangent slope \(m=-\dfrac1{-4/3}=\dfrac34\). For \(\dfrac{x^2}{20}-\dfrac{y^2}5=1\): \(y=mx\pm\sqrt{a^2m^2-b^2}=\dfrac34x\pm\sqrt{20\cdot\tfrac9{16}-5}=\dfrac34x\pm\dfrac52\). For one tangent, x-intercept \(=\dfrac{10}3\) (\(y=0\)) and y-intercept \(=-\dfrac52\) (\(x=0\)). This matches option (B).

143.solution: Coplanarity determinant gives \(-2(k^2-4)=0\Rightarrow k=\pm2\). For \(k=2\) the containing plane is \(y-z+1=0\); for \(k=-2\) it is \(y+z+1=0\). Hence \(y\pm z+1=0\).

144.subtopic: Conic Properties — Eccentricity, Orthogonality, and Intersection
144.solution: For \(y=mx+c\) tangent to \(y^2=4ax\) (here \(a=1\)), \(c=\dfrac am\). With \(c=3\): \(3=\dfrac1m\Rightarrow m=\dfrac13\).

145.solution: At \((\sqrt3,1)\) on \(x^2+y^2=4\): tangent slope \(=-\sqrt3\), so tangent \(\sqrt3x+y=4\) meets the X-axis at \(\left(\dfrac4{\sqrt3},0\right)\); the normal passes through the origin \((0,0)\). Triangle area \(=\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac4{\sqrt3}\cdot1=\dfrac2{\sqrt3}\) sq. units.

146.subtopic: Inverse Trigonometric Functions — Identities, Equations, Principal Values, and Sums

149.subtopic: Trig Identities, Compound Angle, and Equations
149.solution: Let \(y=16^{\sin^2 x}\); then \(16^{\cos^2 x}=\dfrac{16}y\) and \(y+\dfrac{16}y=10\Rightarrow y^2-10y+16=0\Rightarrow y=8\) or \(2\). So \(2^{4\sin^2 x}=2^3\) or \(2^1\Rightarrow\sin^2 x=\dfrac34\) or \(\dfrac14\Rightarrow\sin x=\pm\dfrac{\sqrt3}2,\ \pm\dfrac12\). In \([0,2\pi]\) this gives \(x=\dfrac\pi3,\dfrac{2\pi}3,\dfrac{4\pi}3,\dfrac{5\pi}3,\dfrac\pi6,\dfrac{5\pi}6,\dfrac{7\pi}6,\dfrac{11\pi}6\) — 8 solutions.
149.note: Source had status no_answer_key (akAnswer null). Independently derived: 8 solutions = option A.

150.subtopic: Line — Equation, Direction Cosines, and Vector Form
150.solution: Point \((2,1,-2)\) lies in \(x+3y-\alpha z+\beta=0\): \(2+3+2\alpha+\beta=0\Rightarrow2\alpha+\beta=-5\). Direction \((3,-5,2)\perp\) normal \((1,3,-\alpha)\): \(3-15-2\alpha=0\Rightarrow\alpha=-6\), so \(\beta=7\). Hence \(\beta-\alpha=7-(-6)=13\).
